the presence of alpha-1 norephrinergic and gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) receptors at medial preoptic hypothalamic warm- and cold-sensitive neurons and their role on thermoregulation.
the presence of NE and GABA receptors in mPOAH WSNs and CSONs and the role of these neurotransmitters in the modulation of ARAS thermal messages in the mPOA for thermoregulatory control.

in the mPPOAH, GABAA receptors are hetero-receptors, which are located both pre- and post-synaptically on the WSN and CSN, respectively, to modulate the release of NE for thermoregulatory responses.
the mPOAH thermosensitive neurons receive convergent inputs from the ARAS and the NE and GABA receptors on them are involved in integrating those inputs for thermoregulatory responses in rats.

NE and GAB-Aergic inputs are involved in the integration of thermal and other information in the mPOAh for the regulation of body temperature.
